questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my destination according to the lifestyle I would be experiencing. I think Italy is a perfect place for exchange if you want to meet new people and become a part of the italian culture, since most italians are very open and hospitable.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing and I can only recommend it!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, La Statale was good at informing about the formal things like trimester dates and guides to the university website etc. It got more and more confusing with exam formalities and communication during the trimester, but I also realized that they are more easygoing with deadlines and general university formalia, so you should not stress about it, even though the systems are very different from Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Lots of people searched google for stuff like Spot A Home etc., where people found apartments. Otherwise use Facebook and your network. It is also easier if you are a group of people looking for places to live together.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive and can be though to figure out if it is a scam or not, but it was totally worth it living in an apartment off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We did not have to settle on any courses until a month or more from arrival, so plenty of time to go to different courses and see what you like. After you found out which courses to take, you went to Unimia (the university website) to register and then you got a confirmation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to your contact person in Milano, if you needed any help. I also wrote to the professors in charge of the course if I had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted, and I think most people did.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the first month to go to different classes and get to know the themes and maybe the exam form, so you know what suits you best.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did not find it challenging to take MA courses while being on my BA. The courses were very interesting, but the exams were easier than at home, so I had more focus on just learning new things and less on the final results.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different from home, since the teachers rarely called for us to interact in class. Also much less focus on references and theories but more a general overview of the topics, we discussed. If you wanted to use theories and references, you could read about them in the books available for studying, but if was not a demand for the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Geopolitics of Migration
Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights
European and International Migration Law
Narrating and Negotiating Identities

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the European and International Migration Law to anyone interested in the EU laws and international law on this specific topic. It was very interesting to learn about even though I never had a law course before. Geopolitics of Migration and Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights was also interesting to learn about, especially in a country like Italy, because migration is on another level there, and the associated dilemmas are different from what we know. All courses except from Globalization (etc.) were on a new masters, which was offered for the first time when I went there, so the education was still in a process, which you could feel sometimes, but overall very interesting topics to touch upon, especially when learning about migration in a country like Italy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Apparently electricity in Italy is the most expensive in Europe, so everyone got a huge bill, if they lived in rented apartments.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cheaper to go out for food and drinks, and you get more value for money than at home. Also cheaper to get around with public transportation and train rides to other italian cities. But of course, since it is cheaper, you do it more than at home, so it still ends up being expensive to live like this :))

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could play sports and be in different clubs, but I did not use any of the offers actually.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not use the activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out of town when you have time, since Milano is perfect for taking the train around Lombardia. It's beautiful to go to the towns around Como or Garda. Also Torino, Firenze, Bologna, Genova, Bergamo and Verona are amazing to visit on a short trip. If you like skiing you can easily get to the mountains also. Otherwise Milano has a lot to offer, and you can enjoy the museums or the parks, and always get an aperitivo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough, if you just have patience and try to see things from the local's perspective in stead of your own. If you want to, you can learn a lot from the locals.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had all courses with a very small group of people from Italy, so they approached me, and then you just have to be open and suggest to hang out outside of school.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier could be a challenge sometimes, since not all italians are very good at english. Otherwise the bureaucracy in general can be quite frustrating, when compared to danish standards, and you have to have patience. But it is charming.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality and friendliness of the locals. You quickly become known in your local bars and cafées by the employeed, which is very cute. And of course the food, drinks and coffees were amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: One hundred percent do it! Milano is perfect for travelling around Italy, experiencing the italian lifestyle and still be in a big city, which is more organised than most italian cities. It is also very international, so you will meet both locals and foreigners everywhere.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most BA courses are in Italian, so check the MA opportunities before going.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting local friends and being introduced to a completely different way of living - also way more different and rewarding than I thought. It was also amazing to experience how Italy works and the associated rewards and problems for the locals.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going home :)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
